title: AI borrowing slows as investors grow wary of debt binge
source_used: International Business Times Singapore (one sentence relaying the Financial Times); the FT article itself is blocked
key_facts: Relayed by International Business Times Singapore: the Financial Times reported that AI-related debt issuance fell to about $23 billion in September, less than half August's level, as investors questioned the returns on infrastructure spending.
quote_evidence: The Financial Times reported that AI-related debt issuance fell to about $23 billion in September, less than half August's level, as investors questioned the returns on infrastructure spending.
why_it_matters_hint: Lenders may be pulling back from financing the AI build-out, but only one relayed figure is available.
event_date: FT story 10 Oct 2026; figure is for September 2026
notes: FT page blocked (HTTP 403). No other outlet found carrying this story; the IBT Singapore sentence matches the headline's theme but is not confirmed to come from this exact FT article. Bloomberg's credit column of the same weekend (C07-03) says hyperscaler bond sales are still rising year to date; the two can both hold (a September dip against a year-to-date rise) and are not stated as a conflict.
